title: Fewest Subsequences With a Majority
src: MathWorks OA, IIT Bombay, 2026 (Software Engineer role). Coding question 1 of 3.
body:
You are given an integer array arr of length n. Split it into subsequences so that every element belongs to exactly one subsequence, and every subsequence has a majority element: a value that occurs strictly more than half the subsequence's length.

Return the minimum number of subsequences needed.
inp: The first line contains n. The second line contains the n elements.
out: One integer: the minimum number of subsequences.

samples.ex: 2 appears 3 times, which is not more than 6 / 2, so one subsequence isn't enough. [2, 2, 2, 1, 3] has majority 2 (3 > 5/2), and [4] on its own is fine: 2 subsequences.
Any subsequence with two different values has no majority, so every value needs its own subsequence: 4.

ref:
import sys
from collections import Counter

def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    freq = sorted(Counter(t[1:1 + n]).values(), reverse=True)
    covered = 0
    for groups, f in enumerate(freq, 1):
        covered += 2 * f - 1         # f copies + up to f - 1 other elements
        if covered >= n:
            print(groups)
            return

main()
